chosen.title: The Clause That Broke the Contract: What Anthropic's Refusal to Arm the Pentagon Reveals About Who Really Governs AI
chosen.rationale: Unsealed court filings this month detail how Anthropic's $200M Pentagon deal collapsed over a single 'any lawful use' clause that would have permitted domestic mass surveillance and autonomous lethal targeting — with the DoD then branding the company a 'supply-chain risk.' It is exactly Dawn's beat: surveillance, corporate capture of state power, and the EFF's uncomfortable point that Americans' privacy currently hinges on the conscience of a handful of CEOs rather than any law.

rejected_candidates.title: 99 Percent: The Deepfake Abuse Epidemic the AI Industry Built for Women and Girls
rejected_candidates.rationale: At the UN's first Global Dialogue on AI Governance (Geneva, 6–7 July 2026), officials reported that 99% of deepfakes are sexual and 96% target women and girls, alongside evidence of AI-generated child sexual abuse material spreading through Global South classrooms — prompting a proposed AI Child Safety Pledge. A feminist, postcolonial critique of who bears the harm of a technology sold as neutral is Dawn's exact register, and distinct from the democracy-focused 'Deepfakes and Democracy' already covered.

rejected_candidates.title: Nobody Filed the Paperwork: How Agentic AI Erased the Question of Who's to Blame
rejected_candidates.rationale: July 2026 delivered a cluster of accountability flashpoints — the UN's Independent Scientific Panel foregrounding the accountability gap, a federal ruling against Workday over AI hiring, and Meta layoffs allegedly keyed to 'token consumption' — all circling the same void: when an autonomous system harms someone, responsibility evaporates into the machine. Dawn's structural, Arendt-and-Graeber sensibility (diffused complicity, bureaucracy as violence) is built for naming that vanishing act.
